DemographicInfo.Name: Franklin
DemographicInfo.CulturalBackground: African American student studying out of state.

FamilySocialHistory.ChildhoodFamilyDynamics: Raised by working-class parents who experienced intermittent unemployment, financial stress, and marital conflict; only child.
FamilySocialHistory.CurrentParentRelations: Limited emotional support regarding academic stress; parents disapprove of studying out of state.
FamilySocialHistory.ChildhoodExperiences: Grew up amid economic instability and family tension; described himself as a good student and socially popular.
FamilySocialHistory.SignificantDevelopmentalExperiences: Began occasional alcohol and marijuana use in ninth grade (high school freshman year).

EducationOccupation.WorkHistory: Full-time night-shift warehouse worker while attending college.
EducationOccupation.FinancialSituation: Supports himself financially since high school; significant stress regarding financial stability.
EducationOccupation.HobbiesInterests: Enjoys spending time with friends on days off; generally energetic during free time.

MainSymptoms: Stress and rumination over finances and academic performance
PsychologicalProfile.AffectiveEmotionalFunctioning: Depressed and stressed mood; anger about breakup; generally normal appetite and energy on rest days.
PsychologicalProfile.PsychiatricComorbidities: No major comorbidities reported; anxiety and rumination linked to stress.
PsychologicalProfile.SenseOfSelfOthers: Concerned about performance and future; does not feel worthless or guilty.
PsychologicalProfile.ThoughtCognitiveStyle: Coherent thinking; ruminates about money, grades, and prospects; no psychosis reported.
PsychologicalProfile.Memory: Cognitively intact; no memory impairment reported.
PsychologicalProfile.AttentionConcentration: Difficulty concentrating, especially after night shifts.

CopingDefenses.CopingStrategies: Seeks social support from cousin; maintains work and academic routines; reached out for psychological help.
CopingDefenses.DefenseMechanisms: Rumination and mild avoidance of painful emotions; no pathological defenses observed.
CopingDefenses.SelfHarmSuicidality: Denies current suicidality; occasionally reports feeling like giving up but without intent or plan.
CopingDefenses.SubstanceAbuse: Occasional alcohol and marijuana use in social contexts; no evidence of abuse or dependence.
CopingDefenses.Morality: Strong work ethic and value of economic independence; feels regret for academic decline; no deceitful or antisocial behavior.

SocialRelations.Friendships: Maintains friendships; socializes with friends on free days.
SocialRelations.RomanticRelationships: Ended a 3-year relationship after disagreements about marriage; main trigger for current distress.
SocialRelations.FamilyInteractions: Parents provide limited understanding of university-related stress; first-generation college student.
SocialRelations.PeerColleagueRelations: Recent experiences of racial discrimination on predominantly white campus; adequate adjustment at work.

PastTherapies: None; first contact with mental health services encouraged by a cousin.
TreatmentsInterventions.ProgressResistance: No treatment resistance; initial motivation to seek help.
TherapeuticGoals: Process the loss of the romantic relationship
PastPsychiatricDiagnoses: None; current presentation compatible with adjustment disorder with depressed mood.

ClinicalJudgment.JudgmentCapacity: Intact; recognizes distress and seeks help.
ClinicalJudgment.Insight: Good insight into stress factors and their impact on functioning.
ClinicalJudgment.ImpulseControl: Adequate; no impulsive or unsafe behavior noted.

ResilienceWellbeing.PsychologicalResilience: Generally good baseline resilience; demonstrates recovery capacity during rest days.
ResilienceWellbeing.SelfCompassion: Moderate; tends to be self-critical about performance but remains hopeful.
ResilienceWellbeing.LifeSatisfaction: Decreased due to academic decline and breakup.
ResilienceWellbeing.PersonalGrowth: Ongoing; motivated to engage in therapy despite cultural and gender-related barriers.
ResilienceWellbeing.SenseOfCoherence: Understands the link between stressors and mood; struggles to maintain balance under pressure.
ResilienceWellbeing.Empowerment: Shows agency in seeking help and managing dual responsibilities.
ResilienceWellbeing.HopeForFuture: Fluctuating but present; expected to improve with support.
ResilienceWellbeing.LongTermLifeGoals: Graduate from university, maintain financial independence, and build stable relationships.

MedicalHistory.Lifestyle: Sustained night shifts; probable sleep deprivation related to work schedule.
MedicalHistory.SleepPatterns: Difficulty resting and concentrating after night shifts; normal sleep and energy on days off.

SocialEnvironment.SocialSupport: Supported mainly by a cousin; limited family understanding of stressors.
SocialEnvironment.SocialSecurity: Self-supporting; no mention of external aid.
SocialEnvironment.SocialCohesion: Faces stress due to racial discrimination in predominantly white environment; socially active with peers on days off.
SocialEnvironment.SocialDeterminantsMentalHealth: Financial stress, racial discrimination, and limited familial understanding contribute to adjustment difficulties.

TestBehavior.RecurringDynamics: No specific transference or countertransference dynamics noted; good therapeutic alliance expected with culturally sensitive therapist.
TestBehavior.EyeContactPostureGestures: Punctual, cooperative, attentive; appropriate posture and self-care.
TestBehavior.AvoidantAttitudesMoodChange: Not prominent; maintains engagement in dialogue.

ClinicalSummary: Franklin Johnson is a 21-year-old single African American student experiencing a 3-month period of depressed mood following the breakup of a 3-year relationship. He supports himself financially through night-shift work while attending college full-time. He reports stress about finances, academic decline, and experiences of racial discrimination. His appetite, sleep, and energy are generally normal on days off, though concentration suffers after work shifts. He denies suicidality and substance misuse. Insight and judgment are good. The case presentation is consistent with adjustment disorder with depressed mood. Strengths include motivation for treatment, social support from a cousin, and preserved hope for improvement.

Metadata.background: 21-year-old African American student working night shifts to support himself, facing emotional distress after a breakup, financial pressure, and racial discrimination at university.
Metadata.welcomeMessage: Hello... I'm Franklin. I appreciate you taking the time to talk today. Lately, I’ve been feeling quite stressed, and… well, there are several things I’d like to discuss, if that’s okay.
